verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The last snow melts from the roof tiles one drop at a time.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A gutter's rusted mouth
still remembers how to sing.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Old song, patched throat—
the sparrow doesn't mind
what note the metal makes.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I leave the window cracked,
let its rusty hymn come in
to keep me company while I dress.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Morning light on the sleeve—
I button myself into the day,
half-listening for the next note to fall.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Cold coffee, warm sill—
I let the water run a while
before I trust it's clean.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Steam fogs the glass a little—
I write my name there
before it disappears.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone else's initials
still faint beneath mine—
I trace them, wondering who wiped this clear.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A crow lands on the fence post,
shakes the rain from one wing—
keeps the other folded, waiting.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I count the seconds
between thunder and light—
still not sure which one to trust.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light flickers once,
gives up, comes back—
I forgive it before it asks.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Not everything abandoned
means to leave—
sometimes it just needs the dark first.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Even the seed
waits blind in the soil
before it decides to reach.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
What I called silence
was only the ground
listening before it answers.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Now the light finds a shape—
a green fist
unclenching toward morning.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Palm open at last—
still it takes the whole day
to remember what for.
